rv.q: As far as Hamilton knockoffs go—and there are a lot these days—Fox has actually written one of the better ones, with clever lyrics and catchy tunes.
There are some genuine moments of brilliance, such as Edith’s slam poem, “Yeast of Edith.”
If you love musicals and/or theater and satire or absurd comedy, this show is for you.
Theater 'Slam Frank' lampoons wokeness with jackboots and rap verses while testing the limits of taste (Off Broadway review) Date: October 4, 2026. Author: Thom Geier Taste is subjective.
The way Slam Frank chooses to address it is quite possibly the most shocking thing I've ever seen in a New York theater.
The cast is extraordinary. The score is terrific. The book needs clarity. The premise remains difficult for me to accept, yet, would I tell you to see it? Absolutely.

cn.t: This audacious hip-hop satire about Anne Frank divides critics with its provocative reimagining—some praise its subversive brilliance and theatrical invention, while others question whether its equal-opportunity offense crosses the line of taste.

vr.q: The show is funny. The show is subversive. The show is one of a kind and I think that is the reason to go see this.
